The '''2009–10 [[Süper Lig]]''' (known as the ''Turkcell Süper Lig'' for sponsorship reasons) was the 52nd season since its establishment. The season commenced on 7 August 2009 with [[İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediyespor (football team)|Istanbul B.B.]] hosting defending champions [[Beşiktaş J.K.|Beşiktaş]] at [[Atatürk Olympic Stadium]]. The last matches were played on 16 May 2010.

[[Bursaspor]] won the league beating defending champions Beşiktaş 2–1 at home.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=1213233.html |title=Bursaspor shock Turkey's big three |date=2010-05-18 |work=FIFA.com |publisher=[[FIFA]] |access-date=2010-05-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100521160655/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid%3D1213233.html |archive-date=21 May 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref> They beat second placed [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (football)|Fenerbahçe]] by just one point after they could only manage a 1–1 home draw against [[Trabzonspor]]. It was only the seventh time a club outside the ''Istanbul Big Three'' have won the league, with Trabzonspor being the only other team with six championships, winning their last title in 1984.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/columns/story?id=788198&sec=europe&root=europe&cc=5739|title=Bursaspor claim their place in history|date=2010-05-18|work=[[ESPNsoccernet]]|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=2010-05-18|first=Jon|last=Carter| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100521042549/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/columns/story?id=788198&sec=europe&root=europe&cc=5739| archive-date= 21 May 2010 | url-status= dead}}</ref>

== Promotion and relegation from 2008–09 ==
[[Konyaspor]], [[Kocaelispor]] and [[Hacettepe Spor Kulübü|Hacettepe SK]] were relegated at the end of the [[2008–09 Süper Lig|2008–09 season]] after finishing in the bottom three places of the standings. Konyaspor had to face demotion after six years in the highest Turkish football league. Kocaelispor returned to the [[TFF First League|First League]] after just one year in the Süper Lig, while Hacettepe ended a two-year stint in the Turkish top flight.

The relegated teams were replaced by [[2008–09 TFF First League]] champions [[Manisaspor]], runners-up [[Diyarbakırspor]] and promotion play-off winners [[Kasımpaşa S.K.|Kasımpaşa]]. Manisaspor and Kasımpaşa made an immediate return to the Süper Lig while Diyarbakırspor returned after a three-year hiatus.
